# DotReticulum agent instructions

You are building **DotReticulum**: a modern, native C# 13 / .NET 10 implementation of the [Reticulum Network Stack](https://reticulum.network) (RNS), targeting high-fidelity feature and wire parity with the pinned Python reference so a node running this library can discover, link with, route for, and exchange data with upstream Reticulum nodes. This is a target, not a claim that current parity is complete.

This file defines the project's durable requirements; `TODO.md` is the single active progress checklist, `docs/archive/plan.md` preserves the historical roadmap, and `.github/development-history.md` holds development chronology and verification evidence. Work **autonomously and continuously within the latest user-requested scope**. Complete the requested phase or feature without milestone confirmation prompts, then stop before unrequested implementation; a request to finish the project means complete the whole roadmap. A planning request updates the roadmap, not authorization to implement it all. Do not hand back after an intermediate milestone: iterate, experiment, validate, commit, and move on within that scope. Ask the user only when blocked on something that cannot be resolved from the repo, the web, or the upstream source (for example, missing credentials).

## Project framing and disclosure

This is an **experiment in LLM-built software**, in the spirit of doing odd things in .NET to see whether they work; it is written predominantly by LLM agents under human direction. It is not an official, endorsed, or community-recognized Reticulum implementation. State this plainly in the README (including that it was produced with AI assistance and is experimental), never present it as the work of the Reticulum project or its maintainer, and never claim compatibility beyond the recorded evidence. Upstream's README warns about LLM-generated Reticulum implementations and their license claims; take that seriously by keeping the Reticulum License and copyright notice intact and by not relicensing.

The product target is **high-fidelity feature, behavioral and wire parity with the pinned upstream RNS repository**, not a literal Python-to-C# translation. Use idiomatic, well-architected native .NET: explicit ownership, asynchronous I/O, cancellation, bounded resource use, testable boundaries and trimming/NativeAOT-safe implementation. Preserve externally observable contracts, defaults, failure behavior and interoperability; document justified .NET API and platform differences. Do not copy Python's module layout, threading model or vendored dependencies when existing .NET facilities satisfy the same contract. Architecture changes must serve concrete parity requirements, not speculative framework rewrites.

Audio/video extensions and interfaces absent from the pinned upstream are outside the current roadmap. LXMF (DotLXMF) and .NET-specific telemetry (DotTelemetry) have moved to the separate DotReticulum.Ecosystem repository; expanding them is not an RNS parity requirement. Track upstream placeholders as such rather than inventing missing reference functionality. A broad module checkbox is not evidence of full parity: inventory public behaviors, configuration, CLI options, persistence, recovery and platform requirements from the pinned source, and distinguish implemented, partial, missing, unverified, not-applicable and upstream-placeholder contracts.

## Start / resume protocol (run every time)

1. Inspect state: `git status`, `git log --oneline -20`, the file tree, `TODO.md` and the relevant records in `.github/development-history.md`. Review existing changes before touching them; preserve unrelated/user work and never commit it blindly. If remote history has advanced, inspect and integrate it without force-pushing or overwriting concurrent edits.
2. If the repo has no solution/source yet, begin at **Phase 0 — Bootstrap**. Otherwise establish the build/test baseline before implementation with `dotnet build DotReticulum.slnx -c Release` and `dotnet test DotReticulum.slnx -c Release`; fix relevant red gates before adding features. Documentation-only changes do not require builds, coverage collection or NativeAOT publication.
3. Read `TODO.md`, pick the first unchecked item within the requested scope whose prerequisites are done, and continue. Never trust a checkbox over the code and tests: if they disagree, fix the tracker.
4. Keep going through the roadmap in order until the requested scope is complete with evidence. Re-run this protocol after any interruption, context compaction, or new session.

`TODO.md` contains the remaining phase/subphase checklist extracted from the archived plan on 2026-10-26. Keep it focused on that checklist; do not add chronology, command output or milestone narratives. Record development history, test counts, exact commands and results, upstream revisions, platform evidence and outstanding limitations in `.github/development-history.md`. Update both as appropriate and commit them with the milestone. When later work resolves a limitation, mark it resolved or replace the stale current-status statement; do not leave contradictory claims. `TODO.md` is the **single active** progress checklist: the archive and history are evidence, not additional trackers. Do not maintain session todo tables, status files or duplicate checklists.

## Working loop (per roadmap item)

1. **Define and research**: establish observable completion criteria for the item, separating required behavior from optional extensions and deferred work. Read the relevant upstream Python source at the pinned revision (see below) and write down the exact wire format/behavior before coding.
2. **Vectors first for wire/cryptographic changes**: generate reference vectors by executing the upstream Python implementation (never by hand, never from your own C# output). Store the generator script next to the tests (`Generate*.py`) and record the upstream revision and method in the test file. Vectors supplement, not replace, executable compatibility acceptance.
3. **Implement** the smallest complete slice; keep the build warning-free.
4. **Validate**: unit tests, malformed-input/boundary/failure-path tests, then (once available) live interop against a real Python node. Verify each completion criterion, not merely a passing test count. Iterate and experiment until green; if an approach fails, try an alternative rather than weakening the test. An unsupported test mode must explicitly skip with a reason or fail, never return early and appear to pass.
5. **Review & commit**: run the applicable gates (full suite and exercised NativeAOT publication for production milestones; focused Pester/analyzer checks for tooling; no unnecessary builds for prose), record evidence in `.github/development-history.md`, update `TODO.md` and README claims when affected, and commit with a descriptive message. Check off the item only when all required criteria are met; optional extensions and permitted deferrals remain explicit in the history. Commit coherent verified slices so interruption never loses work, but do not confuse a slice with milestone completion.

Use `/fleet` for parallel subagents when a milestone has genuinely independent workstreams (for example protocol research, fixture generation, separate projects). Delegate bounded deliverables rather than an entire large milestone, with explicit file ownership, completion criteria, focused tests, and required evidence. Require each handoff to identify changes, commands/results, and remaining work. Integrate and verify in the main session; a subagent stopping or returning partial work does not end the parent task. Continue or narrow the remaining work without duplicating completed investigation. Do not fleet small tasks or split one continuous protocol trace; keep tightly coupled wire-format design and integration with one agent.

## Environment and tooling

- Development may be on Windows (PowerShell) or Linux/macOS; use the host's native shell syntax and path separators.
- Requires the .NET 10 SDK. Pin it in `global.json`. NativeAOT needs the platform native toolchain (MSVC build tools on Windows, `clang`/`zlib1g-dev` on Linux, Xcode tools on macOS).
- The solution file format is **`.slnx`** (`DotReticulum.slnx`), never legacy `.sln`. Create it with `dotnet new sln --format slnx`; add projects with `dotnet sln DotReticulum.slnx add <project>`. Reference `.slnx` everywhere (docs, CI, commands).
- The authoritative RNS upstream is `rns://7649a50d84610232d1416b41d2896aff/reticulum/reticulum`, retrieved with our .NET `rngit` client. GitHub `markqvist/Reticulum` is a secondary mirror for comparison, not the source of new reference pins. The current live-reference pin is `a29bfb51c468945c96a1ee22cae0114e993e2391` (RNS 1.5.7), enforced by `tests/Interop/reference_environment.py`. Use a working checkout materialized from the verified fetched objects, and an isolated Python venv with LXMF pinned to 1.2.1. Verify actual imported module paths and versions so `PYTHONPATH` or an installed package cannot silently select the wrong source. Existing stored vectors and their reproduction generators retain their original `e40191b3d193b46b7f2d8a44424a594cd758839b` provenance; do not relabel old evidence as newly generated. Record the actual SHA (and source-file SHA-256 where relevant) for new vectors. Moving the live pin or regenerating fixtures must be explicit and recorded. Keep harness workarounds minimal and visible: disclose any reference-side shim, its purpose, and which unmodified-upstream claim it prevents.
- For RNS-specific research and implementation, use the repository skill at `.github/skills/reticulum-parity/SKILL.md` and its upstream subsystem map; the pinned Python source remains authoritative for behavior.
- On Windows, ensure MSVC tools and `vswhere` are discoverable by NativeAOT; keep toolchain environment setup and publish in the same process. `vcvars` may set `Platform=x64`; isolate that environment from solution builds expecting their configured platform.
- Prefer `dotnet` CLI scaffolding over hand-written project boilerplate. Use `gh` for GitHub operations.
- Language ownership: C# implements and verifies our solution; PowerShell 7 builds and operates the development workflow; Python only bridges to the upstream Python reference. Keep general tooling, fixtures, assertions and topology orchestration in C#/PowerShell. Retain thin Python adapters for upstream API execution, callback observations, actual-import checks, independent vector generation and disclosed reference-side shims. Do not replace the reference with our own implementation, embed Python in PowerShell strings or generate Python files to disguise dependencies.
- Use Pester 5.7.1+ for PowerShell tooling and CLI end-to-end tests under `tests/Pester`, with `tests/Invoke-PesterTests.ps1` as the entry point; xUnit owns protocol-level tests. Exercise separate application processes, outputs, exit codes and persisted results rather than only invoking internal C# methods. Keep dependencies explicit, process lifetimes bounded and cleanup limited to owned artifacts.
- Standalone PowerShell scripts use approved `Verb-Noun.ps1` names with basic comment-based synopsis, description and examples. Separate `#Requires` from the help block with a blank line and verify `Get-Help -Full` actually discovers it. Update all current callers/workflow paths when renaming, including filename casing on Linux; preserve historical command records.
- Keep spawned processes and temporary directories owned, isolated and bounded. Remove inherited `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` from test children unless deliberately supplying an owned output file. Resolve symlinked temporary roots before containment comparisons (notably macOS `/var`); never relax path-safety checks to fix a portability failure.

## Shared compatibility acceptance

- **Compatibility means customer-visible upstream capabilities, not a bugfix inventory.** Expand toward the requested 50-100 major feature/capability claims from upstream documentation, covering applicable utilities as well as stack features. This is a research/coverage target, not permission to invent claims, duplicate cases or implement unrelated features. End-user discussion can guide priorities but is not measured demand or an authoritative protocol contract.
- Write readable Pester `Describe`/`It` cases in `tests/Compatibility/Claims/*.Tests.ps1`, directly driving real candidate executables in a live RNS network. Matching console text, help, exit zero or an internal API round trip alone does not establish a functional claim. Assert observable behavior: actual peer receipt, exact persisted bytes, authorization effects, recovery and protocol observations as applicable. Negative cases must prove the peer/path was exercised rather than accepting an unexplained timeout.
- Use the **same scenario, inputs and assertions** for upstream and .NET; vary only invocation adapters. Keep the actual pinned upstream as the fixed peer in multi-node cases. Execute upstream-to-upstream separately for the Upstream baseline, then replace only the candidate with the published .NET binary on Linux/macOS/Windows. Python used merely as a peer never establishes an Upstream pass. Test both directions where meaningful.
- A live network can stay entirely inside the CI runner: real executable processes communicating over loopback/local topologies are valid live interop. Only hosted `rngit` reference retrieval intentionally needs an external RNS route. Hardware-dependent radio/serial/BLE/on-device acceptance is outside this CI suite; retain it as separate unverified/manual work, not simulated hardware compatibility.
- `tests/Compatibility/catalog.json` holds stable `Cnnn` IDs, **verbatim** quoted claims and one singular `citation` object with exact source path/lines. Candidate initialization checks quotations against the fetched, import-verified pin. Do not silently narrow a broad quote to fit a test; describe the bounded acceptance in its test name/comments and keep uncovered parts explicit.
- Each `It` carries exactly one stable `Tnnn` test tag and one known `Cnnn` claim tag. Append IDs; never renumber. Tests own behavior/descriptions, not a second catalog of scenarios. A count is distinct `It` cases, not the sum of OS/candidate executions. One case passing does not prove a broad claim in full.
- Operational helpers belong under `tests/Compatibility/Support`; thin actual-upstream adapters belong under `tests/Interop`. Python executes reference APIs and exposes observations, not a parallel assertion/orchestration framework or a reimplementation of the reference. Keep .NET-only and mixed-peer contract integration in `tests/Integration/catalog.json` and `tests/Invoke-ContractIntegration.ps1`, reported under **Test**, not silently promoted into shared Compatibility.
- `tests/Compatibility/Get-CompatibilityTests.ps1` is read-only discovery: no downloads, installation or node startup. Preserve automatic test-source line discovery, claim/citation metadata and `Describe > It` behavior names. Execution must discover every claim file through the same configuration, not a hand-maintained switch per scenario.
- The Compatibility summary is **table-only**, one row per actual Pester `It`, with Test ID, Behavior and Upstream/Linux/macOS/Windows outcomes. Link Test IDs to test code at the executing commit, not upstream claim text. Preserve Pester outcomes; no Family column, synthetic aggregate claim verdicts or success inferred from missing evidence. Reject duplicates, mismatched definitions/pins and malformed reports explicitly.
- Optional `citation.uri`/`CitationUri` is verified primary-source navigation, separate from the test-code link. Leave it blank when unverified; no invented NomadNet URLs/line anchors or GitHub fallback. Claim quotations, website manual versions, hosted development head and pinned source are distinct evidence; never substitute one for another.
- Missing prerequisites explicitly skip or fail; failed retrieval fails its Git case and leaves dependent cases visibly unexecuted. Disclose reference-side shims and non-default peer settings; a shim invalidates the corresponding unmodified-upstream claim. Distinguish wire incompatibility from peer policy, size limits and authorization denial. Do not weaken assertions, disguise errors or increase sleeps blindly to get a green cell.

## Commands

```sh
dotnet restore DotReticulum.slnx
dotnet build DotReticulum.slnx -c Release
dotnet test DotReticulum.slnx -c Release
dotnet test DotReticulum.slnx -c Release --settings tests/coverage.runsettings --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults/coverage-<unique-run>
pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Get-CoverageSummary.ps1 TestResults/coverage-<unique-run>
pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Invoke-Tests.ps1 -Pester
pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Invoke-PesterTests.ps1 -ToolingOnly
pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Compatibility/Get-CompatibilityTests.ps1 -IncludeUncoveredClaims
pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/Invoke-PowerShellAnalysis.ps1
dotnet test tests/DotReticulum.Core.Tests/DotReticulum.Core.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PacketTests"
dotnet publish src/DotReticulum.Applications/DotReticulum.Applications.csproj -c Release -r <rid> -p:ILLinkTreatWarningsAsErrors=true -p:IlcTreatWarningsAsErrors=true
```

`<rid>` is `linux-x64`, `win-x64`, or `osx-arm64`. The published native binary must run `--help` as a basic smoke test and execute a representative feature flow, such as an encrypted multi-megabyte resource/file transfer that exercises links, crypto and compression. A successful publish or `--help` does not verify other native code paths; record which features actually ran. C# uses `.editorconfig` and compiler/analyzer gates; PowerShell additionally uses pinned PSScriptAnalyzer with `PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`. Install missing Pester/analyzer dependencies explicitly, not implicitly from test execution.

Measure production-code coverage at milestone completion using Coverlet. Provide `tests/coverage.runsettings` for production-only OpenCover output and `tests/Get-CoverageSummary.ps1` for merging reports across test projects by source file/line and branch identity, counting coverage exercised by any suite without double-counting shared assemblies; do not average project percentages. Use a fresh results directory per run, reject missing production modules, and do not overlap collection with other builds/tests writing the same output directories. Report overall and per-project line and branch coverage where available, passed/skipped counts, and whether opt-in live tests were enabled. Use uncovered behavior to guide focused failure-path tests, not coverage-only assertions or arbitrary thresholds. Keep generated reports out of source control and summarize results in `.github/development-history.md`.

Preserve independent Unit and Integration coverage exports (`-JsonPath`) and their per-project/overall cross-platform tables in `tests/Get-TestPlatformSummary.ps1`. Never add or average suite/platform percentages; the merged report is a union of covered source points, not a sum of percentages. Instrumented managed-process coverage does not measure separately launched native executables. Missing artifacts are unavailable, never zero or passed.

## Phase 0 — Bootstrap (blank repository)

Create, in this order, committing when each group builds:

1. **Build scaffolding**: `global.json` (.NET 10), `Directory.Build.props` (`net10.0`, `LangVersion 13.0`, `Nullable enable`, `ImplicitUsings enable`, `WarningsAsErrors` including `nullable`, `AnalysisLevel latest`, `Deterministic true`; `IsAotCompatible`/`IsTrimmable` true for every non-`.Tests` project), `.editorconfig` (utf-8, lf, 4-space; 2-space for yml/json/csproj/props; file-scoped namespaces as warning), `.gitignore`, `DotReticulum.slnx`.
2. **Projects** (production under `src/`, xUnit tests under `tests/`, one test project per production project):
   - `DotReticulum.Core` — wire format, identities, destinations, packets, `IPacketInterface`, interface manager.
   - `DotReticulum.Crypto` — Ed25519, X25519, HKDF-SHA256, Reticulum token (referenced by Core). Raw Curve25519 uses `BouncyCastle.Cryptography` because .NET lacks portable raw Ed25519/X25519; everything else uses `System.Security.Cryptography`.
   - `DotReticulum.Transport` — announces, routing, path discovery, links, resources.
   - `DotReticulum.Interfaces` — UDP, TCP client/server, serial (`System.IO.Ports`) and remaining interfaces present in the pinned upstream.
   - `DotReticulum.Applications` — NativeAOT CLI utilities and runtime, including upstream utility parity.
3. **Governance files**: `README.md` (mission, architecture table, build/quickstart, honest interop-status table), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `LICENSE` (copy the official Reticulum License from upstream verbatim, with Mark Qvist's copyright notice retained; this project is a derivative of the reference implementation, so MIT alone is not permitted, because the Reticulum License adds two conditions MIT lacks: no use in systems able to purposefully harm humans, and no use in AI/ML/LLM training datasets. Do not relicense; dual-licensing with MIT is likewise not allowed for derived code), `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` (Contributor Covenant), `.github/SECURITY.md`, `.github/dependabot.yml` (NuGet + GitHub Actions, weekly Monday 04:00 `Etc/UTC`), `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug_report,feature_request}.yml`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (checklist: tests verified, interop confirmed, AOT check), and `TODO.md`.
4. This bootstrap is historical context, not a current instruction to recreate scaffolding or defer existing CI. Current authorized automation is described below; remaining work is in `TODO.md`.

## Protocol and implementation rules

- Never invent wire formats, primitives, or fragmentation schemes. Match upstream byte-for-byte; when unsure, read upstream and execute it to produce evidence.
- **Identity**: 64 bytes, X25519 key then Ed25519 key (public and private use the same order); hash = first 16 bytes of SHA-256 of the public key. Identity encryption: ephemeral X25519 ECDH, HKDF-SHA256 (64 bytes, salt = identity hash) to derive token key; output `ephemeral_public(32) || token`. Reject low-order/non-canonical X25519 public keys and invalid Ed25519 public keys.
- **Token** (not standard Fernet): binary `IV(16) || AES-CBC/PKCS7 ciphertext || HMAC-SHA256(32)`; no version byte, timestamp, or base64. 64-byte key = 32-byte signing + 32-byte AES-256; 32-byte legacy key = 16 + 16 (AES-128). Verify HMAC in constant time before decrypting.
- **Packet**: header 1 is 19 bytes, header 2 is 35 bytes (adds a 16-byte transport ID); flags byte layout (high→low): reserved bit 7 (accepted, preserved on re-emit, excluded from hash), header type, context flag, transport type, destination type (2 bits), packet type (2 bits); then hops, then addresses, then context byte, then payload. MTU 500, hop limit 128 (hops ≥ 128 invalid), empty payloads invalid. Packet hash = SHA-256 over the lower nibble of flags plus everything from the destination hash onward (excludes hops and transport ID); truncated hash is the first 16 bytes. `Packet` is a codec only: no encryption, routing, or segmentation.
- **Announce** (non-ratcheted): payload `public_key(64) || name_hash(10) || random_hash(10) || signature(64) || app_data`; random hash = 5 random bytes + 5-byte big-endian timestamp; signed data = `destination_hash || public_key || name_hash || random_hash || app_data`; destination hash = first 16 bytes of SHA-256(`name_hash || identity_hash`). Ratchet announces (context flag set) add a ratchet key and must be implemented upstream-exactly before claiming announce support. Relay increments hops, rejects hop-limit-reached packets, rate-limits per destination with a bounded cache, and never echoes to the ingress interface.
- **HDLC framing** (TCP, serial): `0x7e` flag, `0x7d` escape XORing `0x20`; decoder must bound frames at the MTU, discard bad escapes, and ignore truncated frames. Interfaces are explicitly started and asynchronously disposed; the manager owns lifecycle, uses a bounded channel (default capacity 256) with wait-on-full backpressure, and drops malformed packets. TCP server defaults to at most 64 clients; UDP is one packet per datagram.
- **Lifecycle and failure isolation**: represent TCP server peers separately so routing can exclude the ingress peer. A child disconnect or fault must clean up that child without terminating the daemon or unrelated peers; distinguish this from a failure of an owned top-level interface. Test start failure, cancellation, disposal races, bounded-channel backpressure, and continued service after peer failure.
- **Processing and callbacks**: core processing must run whether or not an event subscriber is registered. Test the no-subscriber path. Callback exceptions must be reported through the project's logging/error mechanism with enough context to diagnose them; do not silently swallow them or let one optional observer disable unrelated processing.
- Implement path discovery, routing tables, and announce/bloom-style rate limiting to upstream semantics; implement links (handshake, proofs, RTT, keep-alives, teardown) and resources (windowed transfer, compression, checksums, segmentation/reassembly, cancellation) per the upstream spec, verified against a live Python node in both directions with multi-megabyte payloads. Verify `rnsd`, `rncp` and `rnx` (explicit authorization required for remote execution); LXMF/telemetry now belong to the separate Ecosystem repository.
- Trimming/NativeAOT: no reflection-based serialization or dynamic code generation; prefer `Span<T>`/`Memory<T>`, `System.Buffers.Binary`, `Channels`, `ValueTask`, cancellation-aware `IAsyncEnumerable`. Avoid platform-specific assumptions; validate each target (Linux, Windows, macOS, Linux ARM/RISC-V, FreeBSD, Android, iOS) individually and document limits. A managed build is not platform support.
- Security: zero secret buffers (`CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory`), constant-time comparisons, never log/commit private keys, credentials, or captured private traffic. `rnid --generate` must refuse to overwrite and create owner-only files on Unix; warn Windows users about ACLs.
- Honesty rule: unit vectors and .NET-only loopback/round-trip tests are **not** Python-node interop. Real .NET/Python executable peers on loopback are live-node evidence for the topology/behavior actually exercised, not proof of public-network, impaired-link or hardware behavior. Keep README/`TODO.md` claims exactly as strong as the evidence. Do not add placeholder tests or workflows implying unverified capabilities.
- **Interop scope**: test both directions, direct links, and multi-hop paths. Include Python transport nodes as well as Python leaf nodes; leaves around a .NET router do not establish transport-to-transport compatibility. Exercise packet loss, latency, retries, channel exhaustion, teardown and recovery rather than only healthy loopback. Record unexercised topologies and failure paths explicitly.
- **Application interoperability**: distinguish wire errors from peer configuration limits, rejection policies and authorization failures. Record non-default peer settings, including LXMF transfer-size limits. Treat LXMF delivery-endpoint interoperability, interaction with `lxmd`, and propagation-node synchronization as separate capabilities; one does not prove the others. If a daemon does not originate messages, use a suitable client/peer to verify the reverse direction rather than claiming bidirectional coverage from a one-way test.

## Historical roadmap and parity acceptance

**P0 — Basic stack, CLI utilities, telemetry**
The list below preserves historical scope; it is not a second active checklist. LXMF and telemetry have since moved to the Ecosystem repository.
1. Crypto primitives + Identity + token, with RFC (8032/7748/5869) and Python-reference vectors; `rnid`.
2. Packet/Destination codec with Python vectors (all flag combinations, truncation, MTU and hop boundaries).
3. `IPacketInterface`, bounded manager, UDP/TCP client/TCP server/serial; HDLC vector from upstream source.
4. Announce create/validate, ratchets, rate limiting, propagation; live-announce interop with Python.
5. Path discovery, routing tables, multi-hop transport; `rnsd`.
6. Links and resources (both directions, multi-megabyte, against Python).
7. LXMF messaging (vs `lxmd`); `rncp`; `rnx`; telemetry daemon.
8. Final P0 gate: fetch the Reticulum-hosted upstream using DotReticulum itself, verify the resulting Git objects, and compare it with the pinned GitHub reference and corresponding .NET behavior (details below). P0 is not complete until this gate clears.

The bounded P0 foundation and focused read-only native `git-remote-rns` gate are historical completed milestones in `docs/archive/plan.md`. Their acceptance required auditing the helper's upstream contract, implementing ordinary Git clone/fetch and verifying local-reference and actual hosted-upstream flows without making repository-wide inventory, push, hosting or signing prerequisites for that gate. Subsequent parity phases cover repository-wide contract inventory and architecture baseline; remaining Git integration/hosting; runtime/configuration/operations; transport/interface controls; endpoint/transfers; upstream interfaces; upstream utilities; compatibility/release acceptance. `TODO.md` retains remaining work and must expand as source review reveals additional contracts; the original phase list is not an exhaustive feature audit. Existing implementations must be audited, not assumed complete. Preserve P0's historical completion without treating it as full upstream parity.

Each parity item needs source references and measurable acceptance criteria before implementation. Verify successful and failing behavior against the actual reference, including restarts, persistence, concurrency and constrained links where relevant. Use xUnit for protocol contracts and Pester for real CLI/process/installation behavior. NativeAOT publish alone is insufficient: execute the relevant published feature. Record evidence and intentional differences in the development history, keeping progress checkboxes only in `TODO.md`. Do not claim complete parity while required capabilities remain missing or unverified.

**Final P0 gate — self-hosted upstream sync:** once links, resources, and request/response work against Python, use DotReticulum itself to pull the reference implementation from its primary home on the Reticulum network (`rngit`, "git over Reticulum") and use that as the way to stay current with upstream. The GitHub `markqvist/Reticulum` repo is only a public mirror ("all development is happening elsewhere"). The community wiki at `https://reticulum.miraheze.org/wiki/Rngit` advertises `rns://7649a50d84610232d1416b41d2896aff/reticulum/reticulum`; treat this as a locator, not authenticated publisher provenance. Confirm the `rngit` wire protocol and request/response/resource usage in the manual's "Git Over Reticulum" and "Distributed Development" chapters and upstream's `rngit` source. Distinguish Git object consistency from publisher/release-signature authentication; the published maintainer release identity is `bc7291552be7a58f361522990465165c`. Build a .NET `rngit` fetch/clone client (or equivalent tool in `Applications`), reach the host through a transport path (a configured TCP/other interface to a node that can route to it), and clone/fetch the repo. All Reticulum communication must use our .NET stack; a Python client fetching on its behalf does not clear the gate. An incremental fetch may reuse locally seeded history, but must prove missing objects were actually retrieved, require nonzero bundle bytes, and disclose the seed rather than imply a full network clone. Validate Git object integrity, record fetched commit/tree IDs, and compare with both the pinned GitHub revision and current mirror (and release signatures where applicable). Differences are evidence to explain, not a reason to force matching trees. Then perform a short behavior/feature comparison against the .NET implementation, separating upstream changes since our pin from existing implementation gaps; a Python-to-C# text diff is not meaningful parity evidence. If no transport path to the host is reachable from the environment, record that as the single blocker in `TODO.md` and ask the user for an interface/gateway configuration; do not fake the result or mark P0 complete. Continue pinning exact upstream SHAs in tests; once this works, new pins should come from the `rns://` source through an explicit, verified reference update.

## CI/CD and automation

CI is an active development feedback loop, not something to postpone until full parity. `ci-build-test.yml`, `release.yml` and advanced `codeql.yml` are authorized and implemented; preserve their separation and inspect the actual workflow files before editing. Unimplemented scheduled mesh/interop/stale work stays in `TODO.md`, not implicitly authorized by these instructions.

### Build and Test

- `ci-build-test.yml` runs relevant push/PR changes on `main` and manual dispatch, not documentation-only changes. Maintain path filters when adding tooling/configuration; negative Markdown/docs patterns belong inside `paths`, never alongside `paths-ignore`. Use only the approved latest Ubuntu/Windows/macOS runners, full action commit SHAs, read-only permissions by default, bounded jobs and concurrency cancellation.
- **Build** publishes NativeAOT for all three RIDs with trimming/AOT warnings as errors, runs help and uploads a commit/RID/executable manifest. Downstream jobs validate and reuse that same-run native artifact; do not repeatedly publish or silently test another binary.
- **Compatibility** runs the shared Pester scenarios with each native candidate. Each candidate retrieves its own pinned reference with its own .NET `rngit`. Seeded mirror-parent history is allowed only with disclosed provenance, target objects initially absent, nonzero Reticulum bundle bytes, strict Git integrity checks and exact pinned commit/tree validation. Record fetched head separately; development head advancing never silently changes the reference pin or proves publisher authentication.
- Retain one canonical source bundle from the Linux candidate, with SHA-256/provenance. **Compatibility / Upstream** and **Test** reuse that same-run bundle to provision checked imports/isolated Python environments. No standalone fetch workflow, stale historical-artifact fallback or Python fetch on the native candidate's behalf. The upstream retrieval baseline uses its actual Git helper. Missing canonical source prevents an upstream pass; non-reference tests may still execute with reference cases explicitly unavailable.
- **Test** builds managed code, runs Unit and Integration categories with sequential coverage instrumentation, then native feature/process/installation and contract-integration checks. Preserve independent suite coverage and deduplicated merged coverage, explicit skips, bounded diagnostics and isolated process summary output.
- Dedicated **Summarize Compatibility** and **Summarize Test** jobs consume artifacts and run even after upstream job failures unless cancelled. Preserve individual outcomes and explicit unavailable evidence; fail malformed/duplicate input rather than rendering success-shaped partial results. Consolidate platform results instead of repeating one test three times as different capabilities.

### Static analysis

- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` is named **Static analysis**: independent CodeQL jobs for Actions/C#/Python, a pinned PSScriptAnalyzer job and a final summary. It replaces GitHub-managed default setup; do not enable both. Verify actual GitHub code-scanning settings/API rather than assuming a missing local workflow means scanning is disabled.
- Keep CodeQL's default query suite unless explicitly changing scope. C# uses a manual real Release build and `CODEQL_OVERLAY_DATABASE_MODE=none` at initialization so unsupported overlay caching does not produce a yellow fallback warning. Keep automatic mode for the other languages; do not weaken extraction or hide real warnings to make annotations disappear.
- `tools/Invoke-PowerShellAnalysis.ps1` scans all tracked `.ps1`/`.psm1`/`.psd1` files (tests/helpers included) with pinned PSScriptAnalyzer and shared settings. Focus on actionable enabled rules, not unrelated style rewrites. Warnings/errors, including parser errors, fail after writing SARIF. Suppress only narrow justified exceptions, never whole test directories or genuine findings.
- Preserve separate SARIF categories, relative source locations and category IDs ending in `/`. `tools/Get-StaticAnalysisSummary.ps1` reports job completion separately from finding counts, with bounded escaped details. Successful CodeQL execution does not mean zero findings. Missing/failed scans stay incomplete; reject malformed/duplicate reports. Keep Code Scanning and artifacts as detailed evidence, not console-text matching.
- Relevant source/workflow changes trigger PR/push scans; weekly Monday 05:00 UTC and manual dispatch scan the full scope. Scope `security-events: write` to upload jobs; fork PRs still analyze/report without uploads or privileged execution of untrusted code.

### Releases and follow-through

- `release.yml` runs for pushed version tags or manual dispatch, not every commit. Versions are the targeted upstream RNS release plus Nerdbank.GitVersioning build height, not a claim of completed parity. Use `tools/New-ReleaseTag.ps1`; tag creation does not push unless requested. Preserve Git history needed for versioned fixture builds.
- Keep expensive additional mesh/soak/hardware work scheduled/manual or explicitly opted in, rather than duplicating it on every change. The existing bounded executable Compatibility suite is intentionally part of normal code-change CI.
- After pushing code/workflow changes, monitor the exact commit/run with `gh run list/watch`, inspect failed logs and annotations, fix root causes, and verify actual uploaded reports and rendered summaries. A superseded/cancelled run is not a failing test. Prefer useful warning-free configuration over blanket warning suppression. Record exact commands, counts, skips, live/native modes, run IDs and remaining limitations in development history; do not describe queued/local-only work as hosted acceptance.
- Keep `ACCESSIBILITY.md` honest about goals, barriers/reporting and unverified assistive-technology support. No compliance or platform claim without evidence.

The project is complete only when all remaining items and workflows are checked off in `TODO.md` with supporting evidence in `.github/development-history.md`.
